symbols.name: chirp vector
symbols.meaning: The vector of chirp factors, whose entries are unit-modulus phases $\chi_m = e^{\pi i m^2/q}$.
symbols.quote: The chirp is the vector $\chi$ whose entry at each integer $m$ is $\chi_m = e^{\pi i m^2/q}$.

symbols.name: chirp position
symbols.meaning: The integer position at which a chirp entry is taken, which may be negative or exceed q-1.
symbols.quote: Here $m$ is the integer position of a chirp entry, which may be negative or larger than $q-1$, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

symbols.name: scaled input
symbols.meaning: The input vector u with each entry divided by the corresponding chirp entry.

relations.quote: Bluestein’s chirp identity rewrites a [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) $F_q$ as a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md) multiplied by chirp factors.
It reduces the transform to a [cyclic convolution](cyclic-convolution.md), so any method that computes that convolution also computes the transform.
The chirp identity is based on the [transform identity with retained permutations](transform-identity.md): the target permutation stays in the formula and is not executed as a sort.
